props.gloss_en: the mishnah: Beit Shammai say one sweeps the house and afterwards washes the hands
the mishnah: Beit Hillel say one washes the hands and afterwards sweeps the house
the baraita: Beit Shammai say one sweeps the house and afterwards washes the hands
the baraita, Beit Shammai: for if you say one washes the hands first, you are found ruining the food
but washing the hands first Beit Shammai do not hold -- what is the reason? because of the crumbs
the baraita: Beit Hillel say if the attendant is a Torah scholar, he removes crumbs that have an olive-bulk and leaves crumbs that have not
R' Yochanan: crumbs that have not an olive-bulk -- one may destroy them by hand
Beit Hillel hold it is forbidden to use an am haaretz attendant
Beit Shammai hold it is permitted to use an am haaretz attendant
Rav Huna: in our whole chapter the halakha follows Beit Hillel
Rav Huna: except this [sweeping and washing], where the halakha follows Beit Shammai
R' Oshaya's version, reversed: Beit Shammai say one washes the hands and afterwards sweeps
R' Oshaya's version, reversed: Beit Hillel say one sweeps and afterwards washes the hands
and in this too the halakha follows Beit Hillel [on R' Oshaya's version]
